title: Erie: which law a federal court applies
question: Federal or state law when the claim is a state-law claim?

steps.note: Federal courts follow a general common law on commercial questions.
There is no federal general common law; state law governs the rules of decision.
Outcome-determinative test: apply state rules that would change the result.
Balance: countervailing federal interests, such as the jury, can outweigh state practice.
Twin aims for unguided Erie choices; a valid Federal Rule controls under the Rules Enabling Act.
Rule 3 does not toll the state limitations period; no direct collision, so state law applies.
§ 1404(a) is a federal statute on point, so it governs forum-selection transfers.
Accommodate both: state damages standard, federal appellate review posture.
Rule 23 answers the question and is valid; the Court splits on how to read Rules against state law.
A Federal Rule that answers the question displaces a state affidavit-of-merit requirement.
